description.value: A year-round lodge and RV park at Mile 497 on the Alaska Highway in northeastern BC, positioned roughly halfway between Fort Nelson (300 km south) and the BC-Yukon border (140 km north) — a genuinely remote resupply and rest point on a major touring corridor. The property sits directly across from the second largest natural hot springs in Canada, with a 15-minute walk along a boardwalk through boreal forest to reach soaking pools that run 42–52°C year-round. Accommodation ranges from hotel rooms to mini-cabins, campsites, and RV hookups, all served by an on-site restaurant offering breakfast through dinner.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, open, year-round accommodation on the Alaska Highway — a well-documented long-distance cycling route — with on-site food service and multiple accommodation types suitable for touring cyclists.
enrichment_extras.notes: The lodge is extremely remote — the nearest town of any size (Fort Nelson) is approximately 300 km south. This makes it a critical stop for Alaska Highway cyclists regardless of amenity gaps.
